topic: Microsoft AB-730 AI Business Professional certification exam preparation - using Microsoft 365 Copilot and generative AI for everyday business work (generative AI fundamentals, prompt and conversation management, and drafting/analyzing business content), with no coding required
exam_format: Approximately 40 questions, 65 minutes, passing score 700/1000, taken online-proctored or at a test center. Question types include multiple choice, multiple response, and scenario-based items; NO coding or lab tasks. Beginner, business-audience credential in Microsoft's new AB (AI Business) series; the certification renews annually via a free online Microsoft Learn assessment. The exam fee is approximately USD 165 and varies by region and currency; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Microsoft pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE', plus short business scenario questions ('best prompt for...', 'which Copilot experience...', 'which responsible AI principle applies')
audience: Business professionals who use AI in everyday work rather than build it: business analysts, project and program managers, marketing, HR, operations, finance, and any Microsoft 365 user adopting Copilot. No technical background, data science, or coding is required. A natural FIRST AI credential for non-developers and a strong companion to Azure AI Fundamentals (AI-901) already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Understand generative AI fundamentals
domains.notes: How generative AI works for a business user (no math, no code): large language models, tokens, prompts, context and grounding, and why outputs vary; the difference between chat experiences and agent experiences; capabilities AND limits (hallucination/fabrication, knowledge currency, the need to verify). Where Microsoft 365 Copilot gets its data - Microsoft Graph, the difference between work (grounded, enterprise-protected) and web responses, and enterprise/commercial data protection boundaries. Microsoft's Responsible AI principles - Fairness, Reliability and Safety, Privacy and Security, Inclusiveness, Transparency, and Accountability - and how they show up in day-to-day Copilot use (oversharing, sensitivity, attribution). Recognizing when generative AI is and is not the right tool for a task.

domains.name: Manage prompts and conversations by using AI
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Writing effective prompts: the components of a strong prompt (goal, context, expectations, source), being specific, and iterating across a multi-turn conversation; recognizing and fixing weak prompts. Selecting the right files, people, meetings, and data to reference in a prompt so Copilot is grounded in the correct material; when to reference a specific file versus let Copilot search. Using Copilot across Microsoft 365 - Copilot Chat / Business Chat, and Copilot inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams. Working with the Researcher and Analyst reasoning agents. Discovering and using agents from the Agent Store and consumer-level Copilot Studio agents; understanding what an agent is versus a simple chat, and configuring/using them at a business-user level. Building and reusing prompt libraries.

domains.name: Draft and analyze business content by using AI
domains.notes: Producing real business deliverables with Copilot: drafting documents, emails, and summaries from a prompt; summarizing long documents, threads, and meeting recaps; analyzing data and surfacing insights (Excel and the Analyst agent); generating and refining presentations; rewriting content for tone, length, and audience. Reviewing, fact-checking, and attributing AI output before it is used; applying responsible-AI judgment (avoid oversharing, respect sensitivity labels, verify claims). Cross-tenant / B2B collaboration considerations at a user level. The recurring skill is choosing the right Copilot experience and prompt to turn a business need into a trustworthy deliverable.

extra_guidance: AB-730 is the anchor of Microsoft's brand-new AB (AI Business) series and is described as one of the fastest-growing certifications in Microsoft's entire catalog, driven by enterprise Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption. MARKETING ANGLE: 'built for the Copilot era - become AI-fluent for real business work, no coding required.' This is a BUSINESS / NON-TECHNICAL course - there must be NO code, no SDKs, no Azure portal engineering anywhere; every example is a knowledge-worker using Copilot in Microsoft 365. The THREE domain names and weight ranges above are Microsoft's official skills-measured outline (2026) - use them verbatim and present the percentages as Microsoft's published ranges. Use EXACT current Microsoft product names: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat / Business Chat, the Researcher agent, the Analyst agent, Copilot Studio, the Agent Store, Microsoft Graph, enterprise/commercial data protection, and Microsoft Foundry - with a one-line note that Copilot branding evolves quickly, so verify names against current Microsoft docs. Labs are READ-AND-DO productivity walkthroughs a learner can follow with only Microsoft 365 Copilot access (write and refine a prompt in Word, summarize a Teams meeting, analyze a spreadsheet with the Analyst agent, build a first-draft deck, use an agent from the Agent Store) - NOT developer tasks; make that framing explicit. Practice questions MUST be scenario-based and test judgment: choosing the best prompt for a described goal, picking the right Copilot experience (chat vs in-app vs agent), work vs web grounding, when to reference a file vs let Copilot search, which Responsible AI principle applies to a situation, and why a weak prompt produced a poor answer. Cover the recurring traps: chat vs agent, grounded work data vs web, verifying/attributing output, oversharing and sensitivity. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including the learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 165, varies by region) and note the annual free renewal; advise verifying current Microsoft pricing. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 65-minute, 40-question time-management strategy. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
